## TL;DR

RepoOS Hub for Android now has a public, release-signed APK path that mirrors the
macOS DMG: a new `android-hub.yml` workflow builds the Capacitor web assets,
signs the release variant from GitHub secrets, refuses the Android debug
certificate, and attaches `RepoOSHub.apk` to every `v*` release. The landing
page has an Android download card with the sideload/API 26 note, the docs site
has a full Android Hub guide, and the nav and getting-started page link it. A
local `just build-android-release` recipe builds and verifies the same artifact.
I re-verified the Gradle release path on this machine with a temporary
keystore: versioning, signing, the certificate check, and the debug-key
refusal. The public release remains gated on the human signing-secret task
(#1129); until those secrets exist the workflow skips the APK with a job
summary note and leaves the release green.

## Work and rationale

**Workflow.** `.github/workflows/android-hub.yml` follows `macos-hub.yml`
rather than inventing a new flow: `pull_request` and `main` path filters for
`mobile/**`, tag pushes for `v*.*.*`, and `workflow_dispatch` with an existing
`release_tag`. A `build-debug` job compiles the ordinary debug APK on PRs and
main pushes so Android breakage is caught before a tag. The `release` job only
runs for tags or a dispatch with a tag. It reuses the same prerelease detection
(`-` in the tag) and the same `softprops/action-gh-release@v2` upload with
`make_latest: false` as the DMG, so the shell release keeps the Latest badge.

**Signing.** `mobile/android/app/build.gradle` now has a `release`
signingConfig fed only from environment variables or Gradle properties:
`REPOOS_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PATH`, `_PASSWORD`, `_ALIAS`, and `_KEY_PASSWORD`. No
keystore or password is committed; `android/.gitignore` ignores
`*.jks`/`*.keystore`. CI decodes
`REPOOS_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64` into `$RUNNER_TEMP`, sets the Gradle env, and
never writes secrets into the workspace. The four GitHub secret names are
documented in `mobile/README.md` for the human setup task.

Gradle does not fail at configuration time, so local debug work is unaffected.
A `taskGraph.whenReady` guard fails
`assembleRelease`/`bundleRelease`/`packageRelease` naming all four variables; I
confirmed the failing release and a working debug build locally.

**Versioning.** `defaultConfig` no longer hard-codes 1/1.0. `versionName` comes
from `REPOOS_APP_VERSION` (the tag without `v`, set by the workflow) and falls
back to `mobile/package.json`. `versionCode` is derived as
`major * 10000 + minor * 100 + patch`, with a
`REPOOS_APP_VERSION_CODE` override and a note that minor/patch must stay under
100. This makes `v0.6.23` produce versionName `0.6.23`, versionCode `623`. The
workflow also reads `aapt dump badging` after the build and fails if the APK's
versionName does not match the tag, so a stale Gradle output cannot be
published silently.

**Refusing the debug key.** `mobile/scripts/verify-release-apk.ts` is the one
verification path used by both CI and the local recipe. It runs
`apksigner verify --print-certs`, requires exactly one signer, and compares the
APK SHA-256 with the certificate in the configured keystore (read with
`keytool`). It also rejects the local debug keystore path. On success it prints
only the colon-separated fingerprint; the workflow puts that in the job summary.
I tested both outcomes locally: a release APK against a temporary keystore
passed, and the debug APK was rejected with its debug fingerprint.

**Landing page and docs.** The landing page keeps the Mac card untouched and
adds a separate Android card directly below it: download link to
`releases/latest/download/RepoOSHub.apk`, guide link, the "not on the Play
Store yet — sideload" note, and API 26. A separate card avoids promising Mac-only
features (Cmd-K, Dock badges, Keychain tokens) that the Android shell lacks. A
landing test asserts both download hrefs, both buttons, and the sideload/API
note. The docs site gets `user-docs/android-hub.md`
(download, unknown-sources install, certificate verification, in-place updates,
privacy model link), an Apps sidebar entry, and a getting-started link to both
Hubs. `docs/releases.md` documents both native artifacts; the root README also
links the Android download.

**Local build.** `just build-android-release [tag]` checks all four signing
variables, builds and syncs the web shell, runs `clean assembleRelease` (clean
because Gradle does not treat env-derived version values as task inputs), copies
`mobile/app-release.apk`, and runs the same verifier. It refuses the debug key
and prints the release fingerprint.

## Approaches tried

I first considered letting AGP fail on a missing keystore, but that error would
not name the missing variable; the task-graph guard gives one actionable
message. I also considered hard-coding the
well-known Android debug certificate SHA-256, but debug keystores are generated
locally and the constant is not a reliable contract. Comparing against the
release keystore — plus the local debug keystore when present — is stricter and
does not invent a fingerprint.

For the landing page I initially folded Android into the Mac section. During
copy review that read as a product claim the mobile shell does not support, so I
reverted the Mac section and gave Android its own accurate card.

## Challenges and blockers

The only product blocker is external: the release keystore and GitHub secrets
are the human task #1129. I did not create or commit a keystore and did not
invent a certificate fingerprint. The guide points readers at the fingerprint
printed in the signing workflow's job summary. Until #1129 lands, the workflow
intentionally ships no APK.

The first handoff failed at UI verification: the landing-page preview never
became ready. The runner had no `landing/node_modules` — remote capture creates
a fresh task worktree and installs only the repo root, so the standalone
landing/docs packages could not start. `landing` and `user-docs` now run
`bun install --frozen-lockfile` from a `predev` script, making `bun run dev`
self-sufficient in a fresh checkout; the READMEs explain why. I also changed
the landing shot route from `/#android-hub` to `/`: the capture gate compares
pathnames and ignores the hash. With both fixes, `repoos shot --task 1128`
captured both targets on the runner, and I opened both PNGs to confirm the
Android card and the new guide render.

I could not run the GitHub Actions workflow here, so its trigger/upload
behavior is asserted structurally, not by a live run. The Gradle
signing/versioning and the verifier were exercised with a temporary local
keystore.

## Key learnings

- Gradle does not reliably rebuild when an env-derived `versionName` changes;
  a release recipe that can be run repeatedly needs `clean` (or an explicit
  version check) to avoid shipping the previous version's APK.
- Comparing an APK to the *configured release keystore* is a stronger and more
  durable debug-key check than matching a hard-coded debug fingerprint.
- The Mac and Android Hubs have different feature sets; sharing landing copy
  across them quietly promises features the mobile shell does not have.
- Remote capture installs only the root dependencies. Any standalone subproject
  a preview target uses must make its own `dev` command install-aware, or its
  preview will never become ready on the runner.
- A shot route's hash is not part of the capture gate's route comparison; a
  section anchor must be expressed through `highlight` scrolling, not the route.
